thread:
jess: Hey team, Acme reported intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures when their private deployment calls our embeddings endpoint through their corporate proxy. Error from our side: "handshake_failure". They say it started after a proxy upgrade last night.

sam: seeing client logs: "tlsv1 alert handshake failure" and the proxy logs show a truncated ClientHello being rewritten by the proxy middleware.

jess: Can you paste the minimal repro and logs?

sam: we asked them to run: 
```
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -tlsextdebug -status
curl -v --tlsv1.2 https://private.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings
```
They attached a pcap showing the ClientHello cipher_suites extension cut off mid-list. Proxy vendor (CorpProxyX v5.2) has a known bug that truncates long ClientHello lists when an ALPN rewrite hook is active.

jess: Interesting — sounds like the proxy is mutating the ClientHello and removing ECDSA/ecdhe entries, which would leave only RSA kx options and our endpoint only supports ECDSA/ECDHE+TLS1.3 on that cert/hardware path.

taylor: Quick check: can you reproduce by forcing tls1.2 and limiting ciphers? Eg `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -cipher 'ECDHE'` and also try `-cipher 'RSA'` to see which one completes. If RSA succeeds and ECDHE fails, it's a cipher list issue.

sam: they ran that. ECDHE fails, RSA succeeds but then our server rejects RSA because the deployed cert is ECDSA-only on that private pool (we recently rolled ECDSA certs). So requests using RSA fallback hit a different code path and are failing.

ajess: (typo) jess: ^

alice: This is consistent with a truncated ClientHello: proxy drops ECDHE ciphers -> no shared ciphers -> handshake failure. Two mitigations: 1) ask customer to disable the ALPN/header rewrite hook on their proxy or apply vendor patch; 2) we add a temporary RSA-compatible listener on a different hostname/port so proxy can negotiate. Both have tradeoffs (security/cert mismatch).

taylor: Eng-runtime: can we add a compatibility TLS listener bound to the same endpoint that accepts RSA key exchange (and has RSA cert chain) and then set up routing so only affected customers get routed there? It’s doable, but requires infra change + cert import.

jess: Customer asked for quick workaround. They can also set their proxy to pass through the ClientHello (no rewriting) or upgrade vendor patch they mentioned.

sam: vendor provided a patch but it’s a staged rollout — they can disable the ALPN rewrite as a temp fix. They reverted the change for a pilot account and confirmed calls succeed.

taylor: Action items:
- taylor (eng-runtime): evaluate adding RSA-backed compatibility listener and estimate rollout time.
- alice (eng-infra): confirm cert provisioning process and whether we can host an RSA cert for private tenants temporarily.
- jess (support): share customer pcap and proxy vendor patch link in the escalation ticket.

infra-bot: Escalation ticket created: #INC-2024-1749 assigned to eng-runtime.

jess: tagging this as P1 for the affected tenant. Keeping thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
